transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I just keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. It's getting really bad. 

Like, the other day at work—I work in retail—I completely yelled at one of the employees just for putting some stock on the wrong shelf. I just lost it on them. And afterward, I had to walk away because I was actually shaking. It really bothered me, because that is just not how I usually treat people. I'm usually pretty level-headed, so... yeah, I need to figure out what's going on.
How long has this kind of irritability and anger been going on—did it start suddenly at some point, or has it been part of how you've reacted to things for as long as you can remember?

It definitely started suddenly. It hasn't been a lifelong thing at all. It's really just been going on for about two weeks now, ever since we had a kitchen fire. It was during our first weekend working on the house, and... yeah, ever since that happened, I've just been reacting to things this way.
Since the kitchen fire, have you been having any unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the fire, or finding yourself avoiding reminders of it?

Yeah, I have. The fire just keeps... jumping into my head out of nowhere. Like, I’ll just pick up a pan, or I'll be at work and open a spreadsheet, and suddenly I’m right back there. I can actually smell the smoke and see the kitchen filling up before I can even stop it. It just happens completely out of the blue.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places, activities, or situations—like cooking or being in the kitchen—because they remind you of the fire?

Yeah, definitely. I've actually been avoiding the house completely. And it's not just the kitchen—it's... well, I can't even look at the mortgage folder, or the herbs I have out on the patio. Anything that's tied to that day just makes my chest tighten up, and I just... I can't make myself go near any of it right now.
Since the fire, have you noticed yourself feeling constantly on edge or easily startled, having trouble sleeping, or finding it hard to concentrate?

Yes, I have been feeling really on edge. Especially at work. If a store alarm beeps or someone drops a pallet jack too loud behind me, I jump so hard I almost drop whatever I'm holding. And it's not just a quick jump... my heart just keeps pounding and pounding long after everyone else has gone back to what they were doing. It's like I can't calm down once I get startled.

Since the fire, have you noticed times when you feel detached from yourself or your surroundings—like you're in a daze, watching things from outside your body, or like things around you don't feel real?

Yeah, I have noticed that. Sometimes when I’m walking through the store at work, it feels like... like I’m watching myself from a few feet away. The aisles and the customers are all there, but they just don't feel quite real. It's hard to explain, but it's like I’m just moving through them on automatic, completely disconnected from everything.

Since the fire happened, have you noticed a change in your overall mood—like feeling unable to experience happiness or love, or having distorted thoughts about blaming yourself or others for what happened?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I definitely don't blame myself or anyone else for the fire. It was just... a really awful accident. And I still care about the people in my life, I don't feel numb to them or anything like that. I'm mostly just dealing with the anxiety and being so jumpy, but my actual feelings toward my family and friends haven't changed.
